title: Room Keeper
summary: Seat mansion guests by who belongs with whom: repair a chart to be reflexive, symmetric and transitive, find the modulus, count the plans.
subject: mathematics
learningOutcome: The student can test the three properties, repair a relation to make it an equivalence, find the classes of congruence mod m, and count the equivalence relations on a small set.

levels.title: Repair the chart
levels.adds: Baseline: an equivalence relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; find the one pair that restores all three (Ex 1.1 Q1 to Q6, Q10).
hints: Look for a pair (a, b) in the chart whose partner (b, a) is not there.
If a and b share a room with someone else, check that chain too.
The missing entry must make all three lamps green.

levels.title: Find the modulus
levels.adds: New: congruence modulo m is an equivalence relation, and its classes are the rooms (Ex 1.1 Q8, Q11 to Q14; Example 6).
hints: Two guests share a room when their numbers differ by a multiple of m.
Look at two guests in one room: how far apart are they?
Check that the number of rooms equals m.

levels.title: Count the plans
levels.adds: New: count the equivalence relations (set partitions) with guests forced together or apart (Misc Q6, Q7; Examples 23, 24).
hints: Guests who must share a room can be glued into one super-guest.
For three guests there are 5 plans in all; for four guests 15.
Guests who must be apart rule out the plans where they share a room.

misconceptions: A symmetric relation is always transitive
Reflexive and symmetric together make an equivalence relation
